extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who appear before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; legal counsel handling USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural requirements, and sanctions applicable to a USPTO disciplinary settlement resolving a practitioner's suspension and misconduct findings, including publication, notice, probation, and enforcement processes. Targets attorneys practicing (or claiming to practice) before the USPTO and OED decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement Agreement compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to resolve the disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement submitted to the Under Secretary/USPTO Director must include stipulated facts, admissions/legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions; the Director has authority to approve the settlement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) (via 10.23(c)(5)) — suspension by state authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct consisting of being suspended from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State violates 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b), via 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state suspension for ethical violations is a ground for USPTO disciplinary action under the cited regulations; such a suspension can support public reprimand, probation, or USPTO suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may publicly reprimand a practitioner as part of resolving disciplinary violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ordered, the OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the OED Reading Room and publish a Notice of Reprimand and Probation in the Official Gazette describing the discipline and reasons; publication communicates the reprimand to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation (12 months) and related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may be placed on a probationary period (here: twelve (12) months) commencing on the date the Final Order is signed, with specified conditions and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During probation the practitioner may be permitted to practice certain non-patent work before the USPTO unless subsequently suspended or ineligible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a). Noncompliance during probation can trigger enforcement steps (Order to Show Cause and potential suspension up to 12 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause enforcement procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, provide notice, allow response, and may request the USPTO Director to suspend the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (A) OED issues Order to Show Cause; (B) send to last address of record furnished by respondent to the state bar; (C) grant 15 days to respond. After consideration, OED may deliver (i) Order to Show Cause, (ii) respondent's response if any, and (iii) supporting argument/evidence to USPTO Director and request suspension up to 12 months. If the USPTO Director orders suspension, any review sought by respondent does not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary Final Orders and Notices of Reprimand and Probation must be published in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette and made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room (URL provided) and publish a Notice of Reprimand and Probation in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner's status, violations, and whether the practitioner may practice before the USPTO during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director must give notice of public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires transmission of information about public discipline to appropriate state and court disciplinary agencies to ensure coordination and notice across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification and affidavit requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must provide a copy of the Final Order to all clients he is representing before the USPTO and must provide the OED Director an affidavit and corroborating documentation proving such notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deadlines: (i) within 30 days of the date of the Final Order, provide a copy of the Final Order to all clients represented before the USPTO as of the date of the Final Order; (ii) within 45 days of the date of the Final Order, provide the OED Director an affidavit and corroborating documentation that the respondent has done so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating effect of self-reporting and client notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reporting a state suspension to the USPTO and notifying clients represented before the USPTO are factual matters noted by the Office when resolving discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order records that respondent self-reported the Virginia suspension, certified he did not practice before the Office during the suspension, and notified clients; such facts are recorded in the Notice and may be considered in determining resolution/sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner may continue limited practice during probation unless ineligible (37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner placed on probation may continue to practice trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO during probation unless subsequently suspended by the USPTO or becomes ineligible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Reprimand and Probation states the practitioner may practice trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO during probation except in cases of subsequent USPTO suspension or ineligibility as defined by regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of USPTO Director to approve settlement and impose discipline (35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director (Under Secretary for IP) has jurisdiction and authority to approve Proposed Settlement Agreements and to enter Final Orders resolving disciplinary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly cites statutory and regulatory authority supporting the Director's power to accept settlements, publish discipline, and order enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 1.3(a) — Diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to exercise diligence in professional duties is a violation (Virginia Rule 1.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circuit Court found violations involving diligence among other rules in connection with respondent's duties as a closing agent in real estate transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 1.4(a) — Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to communicate appropriately with clients is a violation (Virginia Rule 1.4(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circuit Court found violations concerning communication in several matters involving the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 1.15(a) — Safekeeping property
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to properly safeguard client property or funds is a violation (Virginia Rule 1.15(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court found violations involving safekeeping of property; related provision 1.15(e)(1) was also cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 1.15(e)(1) — Recordkeeping/obligations relating to client funds/property
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific subsection of Rule 1.15 addressing obligations (as applied by the Court) was found violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites this specific subsection as among the rules respondent violated in the underlying state proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 4.1(a) — Truthfulness in statements to others
rubrics_metrics.description: Misstatements or lack of candor in statements to others violate Rule 4.1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circuit Court found violations involving truthfulness in statements to others as part of the misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 7.1(a)(1) — Communications concerning a lawyer's services
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper communications or misleading claims about lawyer services violate Rule 7.1(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court cited this rule among those violated by respondent in the real estate closing matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 7.5(a) — Firm names and letterheads
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper use of firm names, letterheads, or other indicia that mislead about status can violate Rule 7.5(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists this rule as one of several found violated by the state court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virginia Rule 8.4(c) — Misconduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation that reflects adversely on a lawyer's fitness to practice violates Rule 8.4(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The underlying state court found misconduct of this type in several cases, supporting discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of Consumer Real Estate Settlement Protection Act (CRESPA) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to register under CRESPA when obligated to do so constitutes a violation (state disciplinary finding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Virginia State Bar Disciplinary Board suspended respondent and fined him and revoked CRESPA registration; the Final Order records the CRESPA violation as part of the misconduct backdrop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent each shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement/order can specify that each party bears its own costs rather than awarding costs to one side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review of USPTO Director's suspension order
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent seeks review of a USPTO Director suspension entered pursuant to the Final Order, the review does not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stay is not automatic; seeking review will not delay the effective date of the Director's suspension order per the Final Order language.
